beats.title: Karnak Temple Complex Begun
beats.description: Egyptian pharaohs began raising a vast riverside sanctuary to Amun that would be enlarged for some two thousand years.
beats.note: Approximate; construction under Senusret I, c. 1971 BCE.

beats.title: Abu Simbel Temples Carved
beats.description: Ramesses II had two temples cut into a Nubian cliff, fronted by four colossal seated statues of himself.
beats.note: Construction began c. 1264 BCE and took about twenty years.

beats.title: Solomon's Temple Completed
beats.description: According to the Hebrew Bible, the king of Israel finished a great temple in Jerusalem to house the Ark of the Covenant.

beats.title: Temple of Artemis at Ephesus Built
beats.description: Greek builders raised a huge marble temple to the goddess in a city on the Anatolian coast, later counted a wonder of the world.

beats.title: Second Temple Completed
beats.description: Exiles returning from Babylon completed the rebuilt Jewish temple in Jerusalem on the old Temple Mount site.

beats.title: Parthenon Dedicated
beats.description: Athens consecrated its marble temple to Athena, crowned with a gold and ivory statue of the goddess.
beats.note: Dedicated 438 BCE; sculpture finished by 432 BCE.

beats.title: Pantheon Rebuilt in Rome
beats.description: Emperor Hadrian's builders finished a temple to all the gods beneath the largest unreinforced concrete dome ever made.

beats.title: Prophet's Mosque Built at Medina
beats.description: Muhammad and his followers raised a simple courtyard mosque of palm trunks and mud brick after their migration to Medina.

beats.title: Ise Grand Shrine First Rebuilt
beats.description: Japan's most sacred Shinto shrine was ritually rebuilt for the first time, starting a custom of renewal that continues today.

beats.title: Great Mosque of Damascus Completed
beats.description: An Umayyad caliph finished a grand mosque on the site of a Christian basilica, its mosaics rivalling any church.

beats.title: Todai-ji Great Buddha Dedicated
beats.description: Japan's emperor presided over the consecration of a giant bronze Buddha in the vast timber temple at Nara.

beats.title: Great Mosque of Cordoba Begun
beats.description: The Umayyad ruler of Al-Andalus began a mosque with a forest of red-and-white striped arches in southern Spain.

beats.title: Borobudur Temple Raised in Java
beats.description: Builders in central Java stacked terraces of carved stone into the world's largest Buddhist monument.

beats.title: Al-Azhar Mosque Founded in Cairo
beats.description: The Fatimid dynasty founded a mosque in its new capital that grew into one of the oldest universities in the world.

beats.title: Brihadeeswarar Temple Completed
beats.description: A Chola king finished a towering granite Shiva temple in southern India, topped by a single massive capstone.

beats.title: Westminster Abbey Consecrated
beats.description: A pious English king's new Romanesque church by the Thames was blessed, later becoming the setting for coronations.

beats.title: Santiago Cathedral Begun
beats.description: Work began on a great Romanesque church in Galicia to house the relics of an apostle at the end of a pilgrim road.

beats.title: Notre-Dame de Paris Begun
beats.description: A bishop laid the foundation stone of a huge cathedral on an island in the Seine, an early landmark of Gothic building.

beats.title: Chartres Cathedral Rebuilt
beats.description: After a blaze destroyed most of the town's church, a new Gothic cathedral with vast stained glass began to rise.

beats.title: Lalibela's Rock Churches Carved
beats.description: Ethiopian king Lalibela had churches cut downward from solid volcanic rock to create a new holy city.

beats.title: Cologne Cathedral Begun
beats.description: The archbishop laid the first stone of a vast Gothic cathedral to hold the relics of the Three Magi.

beats.title: Florence Cathedral Begun
beats.description: Florence started a grand new cathedral meant to outshine those of rival Tuscan cities.

beats.title: Milan Cathedral Begun
beats.description: Work started on a marble Gothic cathedral in Lombardy that would take centuries to finish and sprout thousands of statues.

beats.title: Kinkaku-ji Golden Pavilion Built
beats.description: A shogun turned his villa in Kyoto into a Zen temple, with a pavilion whose upper floors are covered in gold leaf.

beats.title: Temple of Heaven Completed
beats.description: The Yongle Emperor finished a circular altar complex in Beijing where emperors prayed for good harvests.

beats.title: Florence Cathedral Dome Completed
beats.description: Brunelleschi closed a vast brick dome over the city's cathedral without the usual wooden centring.

beats.title: New St Peter's Basilica Begun
beats.description: A pope laid the cornerstone of a grand new basilica in Rome to replace the ancient church over the apostle's tomb.

beats.title: St Basil's Cathedral Completed
beats.description: Ivan the Terrible's colourful onion-domed church was finished on Red Square in Moscow.

beats.title: Selimiye Mosque Completed
beats.description: The architect Sinan finished his masterpiece mosque in Edirne, its dome wider than that of any church nearby.

beats.title: Blue Mosque Completed in Istanbul
beats.description: A young sultan's mosque with six minarets and thousands of blue tiles opened opposite a great ancient church.

beats.title: St Paul's Cathedral Completed
beats.description: Christopher Wren's domed cathedral, built after the Great Fire destroyed its medieval predecessor, was declared finished.

beats.title: Sagrada Familia Begun
beats.description: Construction started on a vast basilica in Barcelona whose design was later taken over by Antoni Gaudi.

beats.title: Salt Lake Temple Dedicated
beats.description: After four decades of building, the Latter-day Saints dedicated their granite temple in Utah.

beats.title: Great Mosque of Djenne Rebuilt
beats.description: Townspeople in Mali rebuilt their huge mud-brick mosque, a tradition renewed each year with fresh plaster.

beats.title: Ronchamp Chapel Consecrated
beats.description: Le Corbusier's sculptural hilltop chapel in eastern France opened, with a sweeping concrete roof and irregular windows.

beats.title: Coventry Cathedral Consecrated
beats.description: A modern cathedral was consecrated beside the ruins of its bomb-wrecked medieval predecessor in an English city.

beats.title: Lotus Temple Dedicated in Delhi
beats.description: A Baha'i house of worship shaped like a white marble lotus flower opened to people of every faith.

beats.title: Hassan II Mosque Inaugurated
beats.description: A giant mosque built out over the Atlantic at Casablanca opened, with a retractable roof and one of the tallest minarets.

beats.title: Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque Opens
beats.description: A white marble mosque with more than eighty domes opened in Abu Dhabi, among the largest in the world.

beats.title: Notre-Dame Reopens After Fire
beats.description: The Paris cathedral held its first services again after a devastating blaze and years of painstaking restoration.
